subtopics.scope: Hardware roots of trust as a historical luxury; the 25-70 dollar YubiKey as a better root of trust than a TPM most people never own; security that ships in the box and works the same for a solo developer as a fleet.

subtopics.scope: A root of trust is concentrated power; the owner holds the signing key, ROTPK, and RPMB write key and no one else; irreversible operations (fuse burns, RPMB key writes, Secure Boot key enrollment) treated like production secrets, never automated past a human gate, with mandatory recovery paths.

subtopics.scope: yubiOS is security infrastructure and security tooling is dual-use; publishing threat models, mitigations, and gaps (the honest cannot-fully-prevent table); no dark patterns, no phone-home telemetry, no unauditable trust anchors; control wins over convenience; security exceptions get features cut.

subtopics.scope: ARM64 is the primary platform because yubiOS can own the trust chain below the UKI: owner-provisioned board root, TF-A, OP-TEE, fTPM, U-Boot UEFI, systemd-boot, signed UKI, verified /usr. x86-64 supported but its lower firmware layers remain OEM-controlled.
